items.headline: Timberwolves Ink Jonathan Kuminga to Two-Year Deal
items.summary: The Minnesota Timberwolves have officially agreed to a two-year, $12.4 million contract with forward Jonathan Kuminga, including a player option for the second season. Kuminga, who chose the Wolves over the Lakers, will fill a key frontcourt need. The deal necessitates a corresponding roster move, with Josh Green likely to be traded to create cap space under the second apron.

items.headline: Stephen Curry, Warriors Set for Extension Talks
items.summary: Golden State Warriors superstar Stephen Curry and the franchise are expected to begin discussions this weekend on a contract extension designed to keep him in the Bay Area for the remainder of his career. Curry becomes eligible for an extension this Saturday.

items.headline: Magic Bring Back Key Veterans on Minimum Deals
items.summary: The Orlando Magic have been active in retaining talent, re-signing Jevon Carter, Jonathan Isaac, and Nikola Vucevic to minimum salary contracts. The Magic are betting on improved health and new coach Sweeney to elevate a roster that sees 13 of 15 players returning.

items.headline: Warriors Add Brandon Williams, Georges Niang
items.summary: The Golden State Warriors have strengthened their bench by signing free agent guard Brandon Williams to a one-year, $2.6 million contract. This follows their earlier addition of forward Georges Niang, who signed for the veteran minimum of $3.9 million over one year. The Warriors also previously added Al Horford and Kristaps Porzingis.

items.headline: Lauri Markkanen Potential Trade Target for Jazz
items.summary: Bleacher Report's Greg Swartz suggests the Utah Jazz should consider trading star forward Lauri Markkanen. This move would open up larger roles for their promising young core, which includes recent trade acquisition Jaren Jackson Jr. and No. 2 overall draft pick Darryn Peterson.

items.headline: Golden State Warriors Crowned 2026 Summer League Champions
items.summary: The Golden State Warriors have emerged victorious from the 2026 NBA Summer League, defeating the Memphis Grizzlies in the championship game in Las Vegas. Yaxel Lendeborg was named the 2026 Summer League MVP.

items.headline: ESPN Projects Lakers as Most Disappointing Team Next Season
items.summary: Despite an aggressive offseason rebuilding around Luka Doncic following LeBron James' departure, ESPN has predicted the Los Angeles Lakers will be the NBA's most disappointing team in the upcoming 2026-27 season. The Lakers ranked first in a panel predicting the league's biggest disappointments.

items.headline: NBPA Expresses 'Serious Problem' with NBA Europe Revenue Sharing
items.summary: David Kelly, the new executive director of the NBA's union, has voiced strong concerns about NBA Europe. Kelly stated that players have a 'serious problem' with the league's expansion into Europe, arguing they deserve a share of the revenue generated by the new league.

items.headline: Deni Avdija's Role in Portland Under Scrutiny Following Busy Offseason
items.summary: After a breakout All-Star season averaging 24.2 PPG, 6.9 RPG, and 6.7 APG for the Portland Trail Blazers, Deni Avdija's offensive role is a key topic of discussion. With the additions of Ja Morant and Damian Lillard, who are both primary ball-handlers, questions arise about how Avdija's touches and statistical output will be affected, and if he can reduce turnovers.
